iOS 26.6 is now available for iPhone users to update. Here's everything you need to know about this update, and why it's more important than you might think.

iOS 26.6 Details

Apple released the first iOS 26.6 beta on May 26, followed by four more betas for developers and public testers. Last week, Apple rolled out the iOS 26.6 Release Candidate (RC).

After two months of testing, iOS 26.6 officially launched to all users on Monday, July 27. You can update by going to the Settings app on your iPhone, selecting General, then Software Update. You can choose to install the update immediately or schedule it to install automatically overnight.

What's New in iOS 26.6

Apple's focus has largely shifted to iOS 27, so iOS 26.6 isn't a major update for iPhone users. However, it includes one very important change that lays the groundwork for this fall's iOS 27 update.

Siri AI is the flagship feature of iOS 27, and it requires reindexing your iPhone. This process happens in the background while you continue using your iPhone.

iOS 27 will officially launch to all users this fall. Ahead of that, Apple says iOS 26.6 will 'optimize' your iPhone's Spotlight indexing to prepare for iOS 27. This means when you upgrade to iOS 27 later this year, the indexing process will be faster.

Here's Apple's full release notes for iOS 26.6: 'This update includes bug fixes, security updates, and optimizes Spotlight indexing to prepare for iOS 27.'

Aside from that iOS 27 optimization, iOS 26.6 is light on new features. The update adds a new prompt after you've blocked too many contacts. The code in iOS 26.6 also suggests Apple is working on a new anti-iPhone-snatching feature, but it doesn't look like that will officially arrive in this update.

Important Security Fixes

Finally, iOS 26.6 patches over 75 security vulnerabilities affecting iPhones. For that reason alone, you should update your iPhone to iOS 26.6 right away.

iOS 26.6 Recap
